title: Dairy-Free Cinnamon Toast Cupcakes
shortDescription: Cinnamon spiced cupcakes with a vanilla swirl frosting and cinnamon sugar dust, ready in about 43 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like the cinnamon toast you grew up eating, but dressed up for a party. The cake is soft, warmly spiced, and made without any dairy at all. I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen to get the crumb right without butter or milk A plain oil base keeps the cake moist for days, which is rare for a dairy-free bake. The vanilla swirl frosting is piped high and light, then dusted with cinnamon sugar just like buttered toast. It is a simple recipe, but the smell alone will pull people into your kitchen.
ingredients: 2 cups dairy-free powdered sugar substitute or plain powdered sugar
2 tablespoons unsweetened almond milk, for frosting
3 tablespoons granulated sugar mixed with 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon, for dusting
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the flour, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl.
In a large bowl, beat the oil and sugar until smooth, about 1 minute.
Add the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla extract.
Add the flour mix in two batches, alternating with the almond milk. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For the frosting, beat the shortening until fluffy, about 2 minutes. Add powdered sugar, vanilla, and almond milk, then whip on high for 3 minutes.
Pipe the vanilla frosting in a tall swirl on each cooled cupcake.
Dust the tops with the cinnamon sugar mix right before serving.
tips: Let the cupcakes cool fully before frosting, or the swirl will slide off.
Use room temperature eggs so the batter mixes evenly and rises well.
If your dairy-free shortening feels soft, chill the frosting bowl for 10 minutes before piping.
Toast an extra spoonful of cinnamon sugar in a dry pan for a few seconds for a deeper toast smell.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes nut-free too?
faq.answer: Yes. Swap the almond milk for oat milk or soy milk in both the cake and frosting. The texture stays the same.

faq.question: Why does the cake taste like cinnamon toast instead of just spice cake?
faq.answer: The combination of a plain vanilla frosting swirl and a cinnamon sugar dust on top mimics buttered toast. Not just a spiced crumb.

faq.question: Can I use butter instead of shortening in the frosting?
faq.answer: Only if you do not need this dairy-free. Shortening keeps the frosting fully dairy-free and holds a tall swirl in warm rooms better than dairy-free butter.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake the cupcake bases?
faq.answer: Bake the cake up to 2 days ahead and store covered at room temperature. Frost and dust with cinnamon sugar the day you serve them.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring the cozy smell of cinnamon toast to a party tray without any dairy in the mix. Bake the cake ahead, then swirl and dust the frosting right before serving for the best texture.
